questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when your motorcycle wobbles. This will make it more unstable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Which formation helps a group of riders stay close together?
questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while giving each rider safe space around them. Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing sound from the rear.
The back of the bike jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of the bike jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You will rarely hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: You should do a careful inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. This usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay beside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the vehicle could block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: Which item provides the best face protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: The front brake on a motorcycle:

options.text: Provides less than half of the braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of the braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: By riding in the center of the lane
By riding on the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves little space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: How should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While a staggered formation is normally best, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. If you develop this habit now, it will be easier to use both brakes quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to operate it. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up. Press the lever down to shift down.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space cushions?

options.text: They do not need space cushions.
They should increase their space cushions.
They should cut their space cushions in half.
They should keep enough space cushions around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should keep enough space cushions around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but always keep enough space around each rider to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look no more than 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, tell other drivers what you plan to do, keep space between you and other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of your lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually for what purpose?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show rules like speed limits. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How should you ride differently when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Follow other vehicles more closely than you would without a passenger.
Brake later than you would without a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start braking earlier, increase your distance from other vehicles, and look for larger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You cannot steer or change direction.
It is only a problem if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot steer or change direction.
questions.explanation: A rear tire skid is very dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you go too fast when shifting to a lower gear, the motorcycle will jerk suddenly and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Reduce speed by closing the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed by closing the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by closing the throttle, lean your weight forward and down, and pull to the side of the road. Once you stop, find out what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, you should reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights help light the road, and their taillights show you if the road is bumpy.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: You can reduce injury risk by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing. A windshield does not help prevent injury in a crash.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, how should they do it?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed safely.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with poor grip, what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder and faster than usual.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor grip, use caution and brake more gently than you normally would.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
On the far left side of the lane.
On the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the other driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Riding in the center of the lane usually puts you in the middle of their mirror, where they are most likely to see you.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.
